decisive_items: Black eschar on the nasal root
pansinusitis along the maxillary, ethmoidal, and sphenoid sinuses
Detected 22 sequence reads of Rhizopus microsporum (0.16% of all reads)
response.rationale: The clinical picture (uncontrolled diabetes, recent COVID, facial/nasal swelling, black eschar, pansinusitis, fungal hyphae, and Rhizopus microsporum on mNGS) is classic for rhino-orbital-cerebral mucormycosis. R1C captures the specific anatomical extent, while R1 is the broader mucormycosis label.

rejected.why: Less specific than R1C; lacks the anatomical qualifiers (orbital/cerebral) supported by pansinusitis and facial/nasal swelling.
Aspergillosis is contradicted by mNGS detecting Rhizopus microsporum, not Aspergillus.
COVID-19 explains initial hypoxia but not the fungal findings or black eschar.
Pansinusitis is a finding, not a diagnosis; ignores fungal evidence.
Pulmonary aspergillosis is contradicted by Rhizopus detection and nasal/eschar findings.
Rhizopus infection is too narrow and ignores the clinical syndrome of mucormycosis.
Diabetic ketoacidosis is not supported; the patient has uncontrolled diabetes but the acute presentation is fungal.
